{
  "summary": "Audit of the discrete fiber-network implementation (network/oxt/network.py, network/oxt/materials.py, network/run_sweep.py) shows that the reported stiffness transitions and oxidative crosslinking effects conflate four physically distinct regimes: (1) topological connectivity percolation, (2) bending- and angle-constrained rigidity percolation, (3) nonzero baseline stiffness from affine background tethers (k_gag) and unbreakable elastin bonds (mu_el), and (4) finite-strain nonlinear stiffening. Furthermore, oxidative damage dose simultaneously adds graph edges, re-closes periodic fiber lines, stiffens bonds, and locks junction angles, while lattice width W is coupled to physical fiber length (W - 1), preventing clean finite-size scaling.",
  "findings": [
    {
      "severity": "high",
      "title": "Nonzero affine background tethers (k_gag) and full-lattice elastin (mu_el) guarantee positive moduli at all dilutions, masking true rigidity and connectivity thresholds",
      "source_file": "network/oxt/network.py",
      "source_line": 155,
      "evidence": "In Batch.energy (lines 155 and 172-173), every bond carries stiffness mu_eff = self.mu * a + self.mu_el and every node is harmonically tethered to its affine position xa = X @ F^T via k_gag (default 1e-6 in build_spec, up to 2e-3 in TISSUES), alongside collinear bending kappa (lines 162-164) and isotropic prestrain (lines 143-144).",
      "implication": "Even at zero collagen connectivity (z = 0, no giant component), the network exhibits a strictly positive shear modulus G > 0 from k_gag and mu_el. Below the central-force isostatic point (z < 4), stiffness is governed by a hybrid of fiber bending (kappa) and affine background tethering rather than a pure central-force rigidity transition, invalidating direct comparisons to unembedded isostatic thresholds.",
      "recommended_check": "Run a background-limit ablation sweeping k_gag in {0, 1e-9, 1e-6, 1e-4}, mu_el = 0, prestrain = 0, and kappa in {0, 1e-4, 3e-3} to isolate the bare central-force rigidity threshold (z_cf ~ 4) from the bending threshold (z_bend ~ 2.4) and the embedding floor.",
      "claim_status": "implementation_fact"
    },
    {
      "severity": "high",
      "title": "Oxidative damage dose confounds topological edge addition with intrafibrillar stiffening and junction angle locking",
      "source_file": "network/oxt/materials.py",
      "source_line": 112,
      "evidence": "In build_spec (lines 112-138), increasing dmg.dose simultaneously (1) adds n_bridge new alive bonds (raising z by up to 0.36 at dose 1 and potentially re-closing periodic lines cut at line 92), (2) increases bond stretch/bending moduli (mu, kb), and (3) activates 6-spoke angular springs (rigid_node) at n_lock junctions.",
      "implication": "The reported 9x-30x increase in G at low z under dose-1 crosslinking (network/README.md lines 96-98, 129-130) cannot be attributed solely to crosslink rigidity or to crossing a percolation threshold, because dose alters graph connectivity z, periodic fiber wrapping, bond moduli, and angular constraints at the same time.",
      "recommended_check": "Decompose Damage into four orthogonal single-mechanism interventions at fixed z: (A) topology-only edge addition (bridging with k_rel=1, no stiff_frac or rigid_frac), (B) degree-preserving spatial edge rewiring, (C) intrafibrillar bond stiffening only (bridge_frac=0, rigid_frac=0), and (D) junction angle-locking only (bridge_frac=0, stiff_frac=0).",
      "claim_status": "implementation_fact"
    },
    {
      "severity": "high",
      "title": "Cutting exactly one bond per periodic line couples physical fiber length to box size W, invalidating finite-size scaling",
      "source_file": "network/oxt/materials.py",
      "source_line": 88,
      "evidence": "Lines 88-92 set dilution probability p = min(1.0, z / 6.0 / (1 - 1.0 / lat.W)) and cut exactly one random bond per periodic lattice line (lat.line), making the maximum fiber length W - 1 and mean fiber length scale linearly with W across profiles (W = 8, 12, 16, 48 in network/run_sweep.py lines 26-42).",
      "implication": "Comparing local (W=12), cpu32 (W=16), and gpu (W=48) runs does not test asymptotic finite-size scaling of a fixed material; instead, increasing W increases the contour length of collagen fibers 4-fold, shifting the bending-to-stretching mechanical crossover with system size.",
      "recommended_check": "Decouple fiber length L_f from lattice width W by cutting each line with a fixed per-bond probability p_cut = 1 / L_f (with W >> L_f) so mean fiber length and degree z remain invariant as W scales from 16 to 96.",
      "claim_status": "implementation_fact"
    },
    {
      "severity": "medium",
      "title": "Batch-summed L-BFGS stopping criteria and eps=2e-3 finite differences overestimate linear moduli in floppy sub-isostatic networks",
      "source_file": "network/oxt/network.py",
      "source_line": 199,
      "evidence": "Batch.relax minimizes the sum of energies across B systems (line 174) and halts when batch-wide max gradient fmax < 10 * ftol (1e-6) and batch-summed relative energy change <= 1e-10 (line 199); small_strain_moduli (lines 249-265) applies an affine step eps = 2e-3 before relaxing.",
      "implication": "When soft sub-isostatic systems (e.g., Col IV/VII with kappa = 1e-4 to 3e-4, k_gag = 1e-6) are batched with stiff systems, forces on floppy bending modes at eps = 2e-3 (~kappa * eps <= 6e-7) already sit below the 1e-6 gradient cutoff after the initial affine step (line 258), causing premature termination near the affine state and inflating G.",
      "recommended_check": "Evaluate stopping criteria per system rather than on the batch sum, tighten ftol to <= 1e-10 for k_gag -> 0 tests, and verify linear response by comparing eps = 1e-4 vs 2e-3 against the exact Hessian Schur-complement shear modulus.",
      "claim_status": "implementation_fact"
    },
    {
      "severity": "medium",
      "title": "Secant modulus is reported as tangent stiffness K(gamma) while topological and rigidity order parameters are unrecorded",
      "source_file": "network/run_sweep.py",
      "source_line": 152,
      "evidence": "Function secant_curves (lines 149-153) computes 3 * sig_g{g} / g (secant modulus), which network/README.md (lines 99, 131) labels as differential stiffness K(gamma)/G0; meanwhile, run_sweep.py (lines 69-70) records only mean coordination z and an Euler planar-face proxy mesh_size (network/oxt/network.py lines 295-302).",
      "implication": "Secant ratios smooth out and underestimate the sharp strain-controlled differential stiffening crossover K(gamma) = d(sigma)/d(gamma), and the Euler proxy E - V fails on disconnected or toroidal graphs, leaving connectivity percolation and rigid-backbone formation unmeasured.",
      "recommended_check": "Compute central-difference or auto-diff tangent modulus K(gamma) = dP_xy/dgamma along the shear curve, and record giant connected component (GCC) wrapping, 2-core/pebble-game rigid backbone fraction, and non-affinity parameter Gamma(gamma).",
      "claim_status": "simulation_result"
    }
  ],
  "strongest_surviving_claim": "In the implemented 2D diluted triangular lattice with collinear bending and fixed finite size (W=16, 4 seeds), increasing coordination number z from 2.8 to 5.0 or applying the composite oxidative damage protocol monotonically increases small-strain shear modulus G, reduces the nonlinear secant stiffening ratio sigma(gamma)/ (gamma * G), and induces mechanical anisotropy (Cx/Cy > 1) when bond additions and stiffening are restricted to a single lattice axis.",
  "decisive_next_experiment": "Conduct a 4-stage finite-size, constraint, and background-limit numerical experiment (holding fixed mean fiber length L_f = 8 via independent per-bond line-cut probability p_cut = 1/8, across lattice sizes W in {16, 32, 64, 96} with >= 32 independent Newman-Ziff bond-insertion permutations per W): Priority 1 (Background & Constraint Limit): Sweep z in [1.5, 5.5] under four constraint tiers at dose = 0: (T1) pure central-force springs (kappa = 0, kx = 0, k_gag = 0, mu_el = 0), (T2) central-force + bending (kappa = 3e-3, kx = 0, k_gag = 0), (T3) central-force + bending + locked junctions (kx = 2e-3, k_gag = 0), and (T4) embedded tissue baseline (k_gag in {1e-8, 1e-6, 1e-4}). Priority 2 (Orthogonal Damage Decomposition): At sub-isostatic z = 3.0 and super-isostatic z = 4.4, apply matched controls separating (A) bridging bond addition (delta_z = 0.36, no stiffening/locking), (B) degree- and z-preserving spatial bond rewiring, (C) intrafibrillar bond stiffening only, and (D) junction angle locking only. Priority 3 (Strain-Driven Crossover & Hysteresis): For T1-T4 at z in {2.6, 3.2, 3.8, 4.4}, run quasi-static shear loading-unloading cycles (gamma from 1e-4 to 0.5 and back, rupture disabled vs enabled). Recorded Observables: (1) Topological giant component fraction P_inf and periodic torus wrapping probability R_wrap(z, W); (2) Dynamical matrix (Hessian) rank, zero-mode fraction f_0(z, W), and pebble-game rigid backbone fraction; (3) Linear shear modulus G0 from both exact Hessian linear response and per-system L-BFGS at eps = 1e-4; (4) Tangent stiffness K(gamma) = d(sigma)/d(gamma) and non-affinity parameter Gamma(gamma). Convergence/Stop Criteria: Per-system L-BFGS max force fmax < 1e-10 and relative energy change < 1e-13; finite-size crossing localization of R_wrap(z, W) and f_0(z, W) within +/- 0.05 in z across W = 32..96. Falsifier: If setting k_gag -> 0 and decomposing damage shows that (i) G0 at z < 3.8 vanishes when kappa = kx = 0 despite a wrapping giant component (R_wrap -> 1), or (ii) junction angle locking (D) alone reproduces >= 80% of the low-z stiffening attributed to oxidative bridging without changing z or R_wrap, then the hypothesis that oxidative crosslinking acts primarily by shifting topological connectivity percolation is falsified in favor of bending/angular constraint stabilization.",
